audit.why: 50.25% over 597 games, EVEN at 4/10, and the text says so plainly ('real WR ~50%'). Levels 1-2 belong to Sion, 3-6 is Camille's stretch, two items flips it back. That is the right shape for a champion whose whole design is surviving the lane to matter later.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike says the arena leaves Sion with 'only a slow charged Q you can sidestep'. His level-6 ability is Unstoppable Onslaught and it is not mentioned anywhere in the matchup.
audit.why: Unstoppable Onslaught is a steerable charge that knocks up on collision, with a knockup that scales with distance charged, on a 140s cooldown at rank 1 dropping to 60s at rank 3. It is a second answer inside the arena and it displaces Camille out of her own all-in. Telling a player Sion has one dodgeable answer at 6 is the kind of confident wrong fact that gets them killed.
audit.corrected: Level 6 restated: still Camille's window, but Unstoppable Onslaught named as the second answer and its 140s cooldown given as the thing to check before committing.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet is right that not one Sion ability is named — the matchup runs entirely on 'charged Q', 'his E', 'W shield' and 'zombie passive'. Two mechanics are also described wrongly: Roar of the Slayer is called a 'shield-breaking poke', and Glory in Death is treated as pure damage.
audit.why: Riot's names are Glory in Death (P), Decimating Smash (Q), Soul Furnace (W), Roar of the Slayer (E), Unstoppable Onslaught (R). Roar of the Slayer damages, slows and REDUCES ARMOUR on the first target, and knocks a minion back through everything behind it — the armour shred is why his follow-up hurts more than the poke suggests, and it is nowhere in the text. Glory in Death makes his post-death attacks heal him and deal damage based on Camille's maximum health, so the zombie state is a sustain and percent-HP threat, not just a body — Grievous Wounds is what actually shortens it.
audit.corrected: All five abilities named; Roar of the Slayer restated as an armour-shred slow rather than a shield-break; Glory in Death's healing and max-health damage stated with the anti-heal cue.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'When his Q is on cooldown' and 'punish the long recovery' carry no numbers.
audit.why: Decimating Smash is 10s at rank 1 down to 6s at rank 5, against Hookshot's 16s — so the trade window is his charge time and recovery, not his cooldown. Framing it as a cooldown to wait for is the wrong mental model; the right one is to bait the charge and punish inside the release.
audit.corrected: Decimating Smash's 10s written in and the window re-keyed to his charge-and-recovery rather than to a cooldown gap.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing warns that Roar of the Slayer can be aimed at a minion to reach you through the wave.
audit.why: Riot's description: if the shockwave hits a minion or monster it knocks that minion back, damaging, slowing and shredding armour on everything it passes through. Standing behind your own wave is not cover against it — which changes where you stand while last-hitting.

edits.before: Respect his charged Q — a full knockup interrupts your E and zones you off the wave, and his E breaks your Passive shield before you can trade. Just farm and don't walk into the wind-up.
edits.after: Respect Decimating Smash — a full charge knocks up, interrupts your E and zones the wave, while Roar of the Slayer shreds your armour from range. Farm and stay out of the wind-up ring.

edits.before: With Q and a point in E you own short trades: dodge the charged Q, E in, W-edge for the max-HP slice plus heal, then re-cast Q for the true-damage hit while his Q recovers.
edits.after: With Q and a point in E you own short trades: bait Decimating Smash's 10s charge, E in on the release, W-edge for the max-HP slice and heal, then re-cast for the true-damage hit.

edits.before: R isolates him in the arena where his only answer is a slow charged Q you can sidestep — your cleanest kill window before he stacks armor.
edits.after: The Hextech Ultimatum isolates him, but Unstoppable Onslaught still knocks you out of it — check that 140s ult before you commit the kill window.

edits.before: His W shield, zombie passive and growing armor let him eat your full combo and live; trades flip to a stat-check he wins. Stop diving and roam off your E mobility instead.
edits.after: Soul Furnace, Glory in Death and stacked armour let him eat your combo and live — and the zombie heals off you. Bring Grievous Wounds or stop diving and roam off your E.

edits.after: Lane start is Sion's: Decimating Smash zones the wave and Roar of the Slayer shreds armour through a knocked-back minion, so the wave is not cover.

edits.after: The Hextech Ultimatum locks him in, but Unstoppable Onslaught still knocks you up — bait the 140s ult, then kill him before he buys armour.

edits.after: Lead with Roar of the Slayer to shred your armour, then chunk you from behind a Soul Furnace shield

edits.before: Levels 3-6 are your best stretch. When his Q is on cooldown, E-in, W-edge for the max-HP slice and heal, Q-recast for the burst — he's immobile and can't escape your gap-close, and the W heal means his tank stats don't win a drawn-out trade. At 6 your R is strong here: lock him in the arena where his only answer is a charged Q you can sidestep, and try to delete him before he buys his first armor item. Don't over-commit into a full-HP Sion though — a landed charged Q mid-dive flips the trade, and his E breaking your shield narrows the margin.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 are your best stretch. Bait Decimating Smash's 10s charge, E in on the release, W-edge for the max-HP slice and heal, Q-recast for the burst — he is immobile and cannot escape your gap-close. At 6 The Hextech Ultimatum is strong, but it does not stop Unstoppable Onslaught: he can charge and knock you out of your own arena, so check that 140s ult first. Don't commit into a full-HP Sion — a landed Decimating Smash flips the dive, and Roar of the Slayer's armour shred narrows every margin.

notes: Two substantive mechanical errors, not just naming: Roar of the Slayer was described as a shield-break when Riot's text says it slows and REDUCES ARMOUR (and knocks a minion back through everyone behind it, so the wave is not cover); and the level-6 entry claimed Sion's only answer inside Camille's arena was a dodgeable Decimating Smash, with Unstoppable Onslaught absent from the entire matchup. Glory in Death's healing and max-health damage also went unstated, which is why the anti-heal cue was missing. All five Sion abilities now appear, clearing the packet defect.
